title: Open cloze: security rules
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: You [1] share your password with anyone: it is a company rule. If you forget it, you can ask IT to reset it, but IT will never ask you [2] it. All employees have [3] change their passwords every ninety days. Your files [4] backed up automatically every night, so you don't [5] to save copies yourself.

pat: don't have to / needn't = no es necesario (está permitido). Es una regla que lo PROHÍBE: mustn't.
items.e: Está prohibido → mustn't.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: You can't + verbo también expresa prohibición y es muy común (más informal que mustn't). En el examen, si la consigna pide la prohibición con modal, la forma más típica es mustn't.

pat: la expresión es ask someone for something: ask you for it.
items.e: ask (someone) FOR something.
have TO + verbo base.

pat: your files es plural y el pasivo lleva be: are backed up.
items.e: Your files are backed up: pasiva de presente simple.

pat: después de don't va el verbo base, no un modal: don't have to / don't need to.
items.e: don't have to / don't need to = no hace falta.

title: Open cloze: the website incident
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: The website was down for an hour last night. The server [1] have crashed because of a memory problem, but nobody is sure. The team should [2] checked the logs earlier. The problem [3] discovered by a customer, not by our monitoring system. By tomorrow, all the data [4] have been restored, and the servers [5] being monitored more carefully.

pat: must = seguro que fue así; nobody is sure indica posibilidad: might / may / could.
can't = imposible; acá es una posibilidad sin confirmar: might / may / could.
items.e: 'nobody is sure' → posibilidad pasada: might/may/could have crashed.

pat: después de un modal va have (should have checked), no has/had.
should be checked sería presente; el reproche sobre el pasado es should have checked.
items.e: should HAVE + participio (crítica).

pat: the problem es singular y la frase habla del pasado: was discovered.
has/had discovered sería activo; el problema fue descubierto por un cliente (pasivo): was discovered.
items.e: Past Simple pasivo: was discovered.

pat: By tomorrow pide futuro perfecto: will have been restored.
items.e: By tomorrow → Future Perfect pasivo: will have been restored.

pat: the servers es plural y la frase es continua en presente: are being monitored.
will be being no forma el pasivo continuo; se necesita are: are being monitored.
items.e: are being monitored (Continuous pasivo).

title: Multiple choice cloze: office rules
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: In our company, all employees [1] wear a badge at the office. It is a rule. You [2] bring your own laptop if you don't want to, because the company gives one to everyone. Visitors [3] enter the server room: it is forbidden. If you have a problem, you [4] ask IT for help. The new laptops [5] delivered next week.

items.e: Regla de la empresa → have to.

might: might = posibilidad; es una regla de la empresa, o sea obligación: have to.
could: could = posibilidad; es una regla de la empresa, o sea obligación: have to.

items.e: No es necesario (la empresa da una).

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; la empresa da la laptop, así que no es necesario traerla: don't have to.
can't: can't = no se puede; acá es 'no hace falta traerla': don't have to.

items.e: 'it is forbidden' → mustn't.

don't have to: don't have to = no es necesario; la frase dice que está prohibido: mustn't.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; la frase dice que está prohibido: mustn't.

items.e: Consejo → should.

must have: must have + participio habla del pasado; acá es un consejo ahora: should.
can't: can't = no se puede; acá es un consejo (pedir ayuda a IT): should.

items.e: next week → will be delivered.

will: falta el pasivo: will be delivered (will + be + participio).
have been: have been delivered es presente perfecto; next week pide futuro: will be delivered.

title: Multiple choice cloze: the Monday crash
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: The application crashed on Monday. We [1] tested it more carefully before the release, but we did not have time. The developer [2] have known about the bug, because she wrote a comment about it in the code. She [3] told the manager, but she didn't. Now the issue [4] by a specialist team. The bug [5] fixed by tomorrow morning, according to the schedule.

items.e: Crítica retrospectiva.

should: should + verbo habla del presente; el reproche sobre algo que no se hizo en el pasado: should have tested.
must have: must have = deducción (seguro que lo probamos); acá es un reproche: should have.
can: can no expresa reproche sobre el pasado: should have.

items.e: 'because she wrote a comment' → deducción casi segura: must have known.

can't: can't have = imposible que lo supiera; ella escribió un comentario: seguro que lo sabía → must (have known).
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; no expresa deducción: must.
mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; no expresa deducción: must.

items.e: 'but she didn't' → debió hacerlo y no lo hizo.

must have: must have = seguro que lo hizo; la frase dice but she didn't: should have (debía haberlo hecho).
can't have: can't have = imposible que lo hiciera; acá se critica que no lo hizo: should have.
needn't have: needn't have = lo hizo y no hacía falta; acá es un reproche por no hacerlo: should have.

items.e: Now + Continuous pasivo.

is investigating: is investigating es activo; el problema recibe la acción: is being investigated.
has investigating: has investigating no existe; hace falta pasivo continuo: is being investigated.
investigated: investigated solo sería activo/pasado; ahora pide pasivo continuo: is being investigated.

items.e: by tomorrow morning → Future Perfect pasivo.

has been: has been fixed es presente perfecto; by tomorrow morning pide futuro perfecto: will have been fixed.
would have been: would have been habla de lo hipotético en el pasado; by tomorrow pide futuro: will have been fixed.
will have: falta been: will have been fixed (futuro perfecto pasivo).

title: Gapped text: the cyber-attack
instructions: Cinco oraciones fueron eliminadas del texto. Elegí de la lista (A-H) la que encaja en cada hueco. Hay TRES oraciones que sobran.
text: Last month, a hospital in the north of the country suffered a serious cyber-attack. [1] At 3 a.m., the patient system was locked, and doctors had to use paper for six hours. It was later discovered that an employee had opened a suspicious email. [2] She says that the message looked completely normal. The hospital has confirmed that no patient data was stolen. [3] New rules are being introduced this month. From now on, all emails will be checked automatically. [4] Employees don't have to pay for the course, because it is provided by the hospital. Experts say that the attack could have been avoided. [5] With better training, the email would have been reported instead of opened.
bank: The problem started in the middle of the night.
The employee must have felt terrible afterwards.
However, the hospital has decided that changes are necessary.
All staff must also attend a security course.
Human mistakes are the main cause of these incidents.
The hospital was built more than a hundred years ago.
The doctors have refused to work with computers again.
The police must have arrested the attackers already.

a: The problem started in the middle of the night.
items.e: Introduce el momento; 'At 3 a.m.' lo concreta.

a: The employee must have felt terrible afterwards.
items.e: 'She says...' retoma a la empleada.

a: However, the hospital has decided that changes are necessary.
items.e: Contrasta con 'no data was stolen' y anticipa las nuevas reglas.

a: All staff must also attend a security course.
items.e: 'the course' aparece en la oración siguiente; este es el primer dato del curso.

a: Human mistakes are the main cause of these incidents.
items.e: Justifica 'With better training...'.

title: Aviso de IT
instructions: Leé el aviso y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
IT NOTICE
All laptops must be updated before Friday. You don't have to bring your laptop to the IT office: the update will be done remotely. However, you mustn't turn off your computer during the update. If you have any questions, you should contact IT.

items.q: What are employees NOT allowed to do during the update?
items.e: 'you mustn't turn off your computer during the update'.

Contact IT: el aviso dice que deberían contactar a IT si tienen dudas (should); no está prohibido.
Update remotely: la actualización se hace de forma remota (la hace IT); no es algo prohibido.

title: Email sobre un informe
instructions: Leé el mensaje y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
To: Tom
Subject: Missing report
Hi Tom, the client says the report was sent yesterday, but we can't find it. Could you check whether it was sent to the right address? It may have gone to spam. Thanks!

items.q: What does the writer think may have happened?
o: The report may be in the spam folder
The client never wrote a report
items.a: The report may be in the spam folder
items.e: 'It may have gone to spam'.

The client never wrote a report: el cliente dice que el informe fue enviado; no habla de que no lo escribió.
Tom deleted it on purpose: el texto no acusa a Tom; sugiere que pudo haber ido a spam.

title: The security audit
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta para cada pregunta.
text:
Last week, an external company reviewed the security of Nova Systems, a software company with three hundred employees. The audit lasted five days, and the results were presented on Friday.
According to the report, the technical part of the system is well protected. All data is stored in encrypted servers, and every change is recorded automatically. However, the auditors found several problems with human behaviour. Some employees share passwords with colleagues, and others use the same password for all their accounts. "This mustn't happen," the head auditor explained. "One stolen password can open the door to the whole company."
The company has reacted quickly. New rules are being prepared, and a training course will be offered to everyone. Employees who already know the basics don't have to attend, but they should read the new guide. The company's director admitted that the audit should have been done years ago. "We were lucky nothing serious happened," she said. "It could have been a disaster."
The changes will have been completed by the end of the year, and a second audit is planned for next spring.

items.q: What did the audit find about the technical system?
items.e: 'the technical part of the system is well protected'.

It has to be replaced: el informe dice que la parte técnica está bien protegida; no habla de reemplazarla.
It was hacked: no hubo un ataque; la auditoría la revisó y encontró que está bien protegida.

items.q: What problem did the auditors find?
items.e: 'share passwords ... use the same password for all their accounts'.

The servers have no backups: no se menciona la falta de backups; el problema es el comportamiento humano.
Nobody uses encryption: dice que los datos están en servidores cifrados.

items.q: Who doesn't have to attend the training course?
o: Employees who already know the basics
items.a: Employees who already know the basics
items.e: 'Employees who already know the basics don't have to attend'.

The directors: no se menciona a los directivos; los que no tienen que asistir son los que ya saben lo básico.
New employees: no se dice eso; el curso se ofrece a todos.

items.q: What does the director say about the audit?
o: It should have been done earlier
items.a: It should have been done earlier
items.e: 'the audit should have been done years ago'.

It was unnecessary: dice lo contrario: debería haberse hecho años atrás.
It cost too much: no se habla del costo de la auditoría.

items.q: What is planned for next spring?
items.e: 'a second audit is planned for next spring'.

The end of the training: lo que se planea para la próxima primavera es una segunda auditoría.
A new office: no se menciona ninguna oficina nueva.

title: Programmers and AI tools
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text: Many people believe that artificial intelligence will soon be able to write all software, but experienced programmers are not convinced. AI tools can generate code quickly, and they are already being used by thousands of developers. However, the code they produce must be reviewed carefully, because it may contain errors that are difficult to notice. Some companies have already suffered problems that could have been avoided if the code had been checked by a human. For this reason, many experts argue that programmers should learn to work with these tools rather than fear them. A developer who can explain what a piece of code does, and why it might fail, is unlikely to be replaced.

items.q: Why must code produced by AI be reviewed?
o: It may contain errors that are hard to notice
It cannot be read by humans
items.a: It may contain errors that are hard to notice
items.e: 'it may contain errors that are difficult to notice'.

It is always too slow: dice que las herramientas generan código rápido.
It cannot be read by humans: no se dice eso; el problema es que puede tener errores difíciles de notar.
It is illegal: no se menciona nada de legalidad.

o: Programmers should learn to work with AI tools
items.a: Programmers should learn to work with AI tools
items.e: 'programmers should learn to work with these tools rather than fear them'.

Programmers should stop learning: dice lo contrario: deberían aprender a trabajar con estas herramientas.
Companies should ban AI: no recomiendan prohibirla; recomiendan aprender a usarla.
Humans should never check code: dice que el código debe ser revisado por una persona.
